headline: House Disclosure Puts Numbers on China AI-Chip Licences
deck: The release identifies applicants and approvals, while leaving actual China-bound shipments unresolved.
body: House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast used authority under the Export Control Reform Act to release information about Nvidia and AMD AI-chip licence applications concerning China. The House release says the applications sought sales of 3.4 million AI chips and the Bureau of Industry and Security approved more than 879,000 [E1][E2].

The House release also says the information includes requests by Nvidia to depend on possible chip-smuggling fronts to facilitate sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies [E3]. Representative Gregory Meeks, the committee’s ranking member, said the committee unanimously approved disclosure of Bureau of Industry and Security licensing information on Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips [E4]. Meeks said the disclosure would inform the public about how the agency handled the licences, and said the agency appeared to approve advanced-chip licences for China with little scrutiny [E5][E6].

Channel News Asia and Reuters reported the House committee’s account of approvals from December 2025 through May 2026 [E7][E10]. Channel News Asia reported that the approvals included 150,000 chips for Tencent, 75,000 for Alibaba, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, which the committee said were on the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies [E8].

Channel News Asia reported that the documents did not make clear how many approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments, which would have included Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips [E9]. Nvidia said the approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes [E11].
The disclosure adds published application and approval counts to a House request for Nvidia and Commerce briefings over Megaspeed and national-security concerns [E12].
